**Proposed mechanism:** NDUFB11 (HGNC:7702) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial Complex I Assembly (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial Complex I Assembly (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complex I Activity (GO:0005751); Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complex I Activity (GO:0005751) —DECREASES→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001299); Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complex I Activity (GO:0005751) —DECREASES→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); NDUFA2 (HGNC:7663) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial Complex I Assembly (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complex I Activity (GO:0005751) —DECREASES→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Mutations in NDUFB11 (HGNC:7702), a gene implicated in both disease A and disease B, disrupt the assembly of mitochondrial complex I (GO:0005759). This leads to impaired electron transport chain complex I activity (GO:0005751), ultimately causing a decrease in complex I function. The downstream consequences of this functional deficit manifest as severe neurological phenotypes such as encephalopathy (HP:0001299), hypotonia (HP:0001252), and developmental delay (HP:0001263).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NDUFB11 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in either disease, or evidence that the causal variants for disease B do not affect NDUFB11 or its role in complex I assembly. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis and mechanistic overlap in mitochondrial complex I deficiencies, particularly those involving NDUFB11, can guide diagnostic efforts and potentially lead to targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at improving mitochondrial function or mitigating downstream consequences for patients with these debilitating disorders.
